summary: Second review. First head 205089c8 was REFUSED by me: fleet_health_cron.sh fingerprinted FLEET_RUNTIME by check name, one FP for nine services, so while any unit was RED (momentum-paper is deliberately stopped today) a later OMS/v2 crash loop could never page. At 56ee2922: rows are per service AND per condition (service-runtime:<slug>:inactive / :restart-storm / :maintenance-expired), the wrapper FP is derived from that row name, so recovery clears only its own FP. Maintenance file added: <unit> <until-ISO8601-UTC> <reason>; active window reports MAINTENANCE (never GREEN, never pages), expired window pages, malformed/unknown/duplicate lines page as maintenance-file:invalid, open-ended entries rejected. Read the full range diff (2 codex-marked commits) and the unchanged wrapper dedupe loop. Ran 50/50 (test_fleet_health.py + test_fleet_health_cron.py) from the PR worktree. MY OWN MUTATIONS: M1 collapse every row name to one slug -> 4 RED incl. test_runtime_rows_are_independent_per_service_and_condition; M2 maintenance never expires -> RED; M4 wrapper no longer pages FLEET_RUNTIME -> 4 RED incl. test_existing_momentum_red_does_not_mask_a_later_oms_red, test_oms_recovery_clears_only_oms_fingerprint..., test_same_service_flap_pages_on_each_new_red_transition. M3 SURVIVES (remove the 'expiry must be UTC' guard -> 50/50 green): accepted because the consequence is nil on this box (a naive time is read as local = UTC and still expires) - follow-up test requested, not blocking. Also noted, not blocking: classify_service_restarts() is now dead production code kept alive only by 3 unit tests; a crash INSIDE the runtime check degrades to AMBER (silent) by the runner's existing design, only systemctl-unreadable is an explicit RED. Could NOT verify: ntfy delivery (the send function logs no receipt - separate finding), and the root-crontab install; both are deploy-time checks.
